hook: Thousands of lost negatives were found hidden inside suitcases at Leiden University Libraries.

sections.voiceover: Thousands of lost negatives were found hidden inside suitcases at Leiden University Libraries.
sections.visual_cue: Close-up of vintage worn suitcases sitting on a library table, slightly open to reveal contents.
sections.sfx_cue: Soft, muffled sound of a latch clicking open.

sections.voiceover: Inside those cases rested the life work of resistance fighter and photographer Violette Cornelius. Did this Nieuwe Kunstschool student in Amsterdam capture her life from 1919 to 1998?
sections.visual_cue: Archival black and white portraits of Violette Cornelius and shots of the Nieuwe Kunstschool.
sections.sfx_cue: Quiet, rhythmic sound of a film shutter clicking.

sections.voiceover: These negatives reveal her secret resistance work, proving she risked everything during the war.
sections.visual_cue: Macro shot of a stack of old photographic negatives held up to light.
sections.sfx_cue: Sound of paper sliding against paper.

sections.voiceover: The Nederlands Fotomuseum now answers that question with the exhibition Violette Cornelius Rediscovered. You can view the collection from November 20, 2026, through February 28, 2027.
sections.visual_cue: Interior shot of the Nederlands Fotomuseum gallery walls displaying large prints.
sections.sfx_cue: Echoing footsteps in a quiet gallery space.

sections.voiceover: Visit the Nederlands Fotomuseum to see these 200 works from the suitcases.
sections.visual_cue: Slow zoom in on a single evocative photograph from the collection.
b_roll: Close up of a historical photograph
